months: periods that a year is divided into, plural of month
It took several months for the wound to heal completely.
choosing: the act of selecting one thing from a number of possibilities
Choosing the right career path takes time and honest reflection.
fits: is the right size, shape, or type for something
This solution fits our budget better than the other option.
area: a particular part of a place, or the size of a surface
The park covers a large area near the edge of town.
instead: He skipped dinner and had a light snack instead.
forcing: making someone or something do a particular thing
The drought is forcing farmers to sell part of their herds.
everywhere: in, at, or to all places
It is controlled movement: letting the structure shift everywhere it needs to.
adaptation: the process of adjusting to new conditions
The species shows remarkable adaptation to extreme desert heat.
limits: the greatest amounts or extents allowed
Every method of measuring risk has its own limits.
die: to stop living, or to gradually fade and stop
The applause slowly began to die as the lights dimmed.
disease: an illness affecting a person, animal, or plant
Doctors are working to find a cure for the rare disease.
spreads: extends over a larger area or reaches more people over time
News spreads quickly on social media these days.
every: used to refer to each member of a group without exception
Somebody must repaint the roof every few years.
afford: to have enough money or resources to be able to do something
Few young families can afford to buy a house downtown now.
experts: people with great knowledge or skill in a particular area
Many experts are careful with the word 'crisis'.
argue: to give reasons to support an opinion, or to disagree
The siblings often argue about whose turn it is to cook.
future: the period of time that is to come
Nobody can predict exactly what the future holds.
depends: is affected or determined by something
The success of the picnic depends entirely on the weather.
decisions: choices or judgments made after considering options
Difficult decisions about funding are made by the board each year.
made: The table was made entirely from reclaimed wood.
elsewhere: in, at, or to another place
If this shop can't help, try looking elsewhere in town.
how: She explained how the machine works in simple terms.
pumped: moved using a machine or force
Thousands of litres of floodwater were pumped out of the basement overnight.
managed: succeeded in doing something, or controlled it
Somehow the small team managed to finish the project on time.
cannot: used to say that something is not possible or not allowed
Visitors cannot enter the site without prior written permission.
bring: to carry or take something to a place, or to start a legal case
Lawyers plan to bring a case against the company next month.
back: returning to a previous place, position or condition
She promised to call him back as soon as she landed.
